props.title: Moulin Rouge!
props.initialSlug: A love story for the ages.

sections.content: Baz Luhrmann's Moulin Rouge! revolutionized the modern movie musical with its frenetic "pop mashup" approach. The film's audacious blend of contemporary hits like "Lady Marmalade" and "Your Song" with the belle époque setting created a template that influenced everything from Chicago (2002) to The Greatest Showman (2017). Luhrmann's signature "Red Curtain Trilogy" style, which began with Strictly Ballroom (1992) and Romeo + Juliet (1996), reached its apex here - combining rapid-fire editing, saturated colors, and theatrical artifice to create a delirious cinematic spectacle.

sections.content: Nicole Kidman and Ewan McGregor's performances ground the film's elaborate fantasy in genuine emotion. Their rendition of "Come What May" (the film's only original song) provides the emotional anchor amid the swirling mashups. The film's influence extends beyond musicals - its rapid montage style and anachronistic music choices echo in works like Marie Antoinette (2006) and The Great Gatsby (2013), another Luhrmann spectacle that applies similar techniques to F. Scott Fitzgerald's classic.

The film's production design by Catherine Martin (who won an Oscar) creates a heightened, fantastical version of 1899 Paris that draws from both historical reference and pure imagination. This approach influenced later period musicals like Sweeney Todd (2007) and Les Misérables (2012), which similarly balance historical accuracy with theatrical stylization. The iconic red windmill and elephant room remain some of cinema's most memorable sets. SUBHEAD: The Musical Revolution

sections.content: Moulin Rouge! marked a crucial turning point for movie musicals, which had largely fallen out of favor since the 1960s. Its success paved the way for the genre's revival, influencing films like La La Land (2016) and In the Heights (2021). The film's innovative approach to incorporating pop music - from Nirvana to Madonna - created a new template for jukebox musicals like Mamma Mia! (2008) and Rock of Ages (2012).
